mainTopic: Beehives and leaks on שבת, removing disgusting things, and acts forbidden on both שבת and יום טוב
overview: The גמרא finishes the ברייתא about covering a beehive on שבת: you may cover it, as long as the covering does not become a trap. רב אשי reads the seasons in the ברייתא as ניסן and תשרי, when there is honey in the hive. Next comes the משנה's rule that you may put a vessel under a leak and empty it again and again. A story tells how רבה told אביי to bring his bed into his leaking millhouse, so the water would count like a גרף של רעי (chamber pot) and could be removed. אביי questioned this, and his millhouse collapsed. שמואל then rules on carrying out chamber pots, and a story about רב אשי and a mouse shows that disgusting things may be removed even without a vessel. A new משנה teaches that acts forbidden on שבת as שבות, רשות, or מצוה are also forbidden on יום טוב, and that the only difference between the days is אוכל נפש. The גמרא explains the reason for each שבות decree. It then starts asking why judging and betrothal are called only רשות, and the answer about betrothal continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Rewording the ברייתא: just don't make the mat into a trap
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rewords the end of the ברייתא. Instead of 'as long as he does not intend to trap,' it reads 'as long as he does not make it a trap.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say this: As long as he does not make it into a trap.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the wording of the ברייתא. The condition is now that the person must not cover the hive in a way that turns it into a trap for the bees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the wording 'as long as he does not intend to trap' caused a difficulty. The new wording moves the focus from what the person intends to what he actually does. He may cover the hive, but he must not close it up so fully that the bees are caught inside.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, say: the גמרא is changing how a source should be read
As long as / on condition that

phrases.english: Rather, say:
As long as he does not make it a trap.
phrases.notes: 'It' is the mat spread over the hive. He should not cover it so fully that the bees can't get out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the earlier difficulty (before this section) with the wording 'as long as he does not intend to trap'.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא was about the person's intention to trap.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about what he does: he must not make the covering into an actual trap.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא would need to tell us not to trap the bees. Trapping on שבת is clearly forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new wording. Everyone knows you may not trap on שבת, so why would the ברייתא bother saying it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ברייתא is not supposed to teach something that adds no new information. If 'don't make it a trap' only repeats the basic rule against צידה, it seems to be an empty line.

keyTerms.meaning: It's obvious! (a challenge that a teaching adds nothing new)

phrases.english: It's obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the rewording given in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reworded line 'as long as he does not make it a trap.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Trapping is clearly forbidden on שבת, so saying it adds nothing.

steps.title: Even creatures people don't usually trap may not be trapped
steps.stepSummary: The line is needed. Otherwise we might think only creatures that people normally hunt are forbidden to trap. The ברייתא teaches that bees may not be trapped either.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: a creature whose kind is usually trapped is forbidden, but one whose kind is not usually trapped is permitted. So it teaches us that this is not so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing what we might have mistakenly thought without this line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bees are not a creature people usually go out to hunt. So one might think trapping them is not real צידה and is allowed. The ברייתא's warning tells us that even bees may not be trapped.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (introduces a mistaken idea we could have had)
It teaches us (that the mistaken idea is wrong)

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא allows covering a beehive on שבת, as long as the covering does not turn into a trap. This holds even though bees are not usually hunted.

phrases.english: You might have said:
A creature whose kind is trapped is forbidden,
one whose kind is not trapped is permitted,
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'obvious' challenge of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing a mistaken idea we could have had (מהו דתימא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only creatures that are normally hunted are forbidden to trap. Bees would be allowed.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even bees, which are not normally hunted, may not be trapped on שבת.

steps.title: רב אשי: the ברייתא means Nisan and Tishrei, when there is honey
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the ברייתא does not speak of summer and the rainy season. It says 'in the sun because of the sun, in the rain because of the rain.' That fits ניסן and תשרי, when there is sun, rain, and also honey in the hive.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Does the ברייתא say 'in the summer days and in the rainy days'? It says 'in the sun because of the sun and in the rain because of the rain.' It means the days of ניסן and the days of תשרי, when there is sun, there is rain, and there is honey.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי goes back to an earlier question about the seasons in the ברייתא. He reads the ברייתא more carefully to show it is talking about times when there is honey in the hive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier it seemed the ברייתא spoke of summer and winter, when the hive has no honey. רב אשי points out that the ברייתא only says 'sun' and 'rain', not 'seasons.' That fits ניסן and תשרי, when the hive does have honey, so the earlier explanation based on the honey can stand.

keyTerms.meaning: Does it actually teach...? (a check of the exact wording)

steps.confusionAlert: רב אשי is not answering the 'obvious' question from steps 2-3. He is going back to the earlier issue of the seasons and the honey.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:

phrases.aramaic: מִי קָתָנֵי בִּימוֹת הַחַמָּה וּבִימוֹת הַגְּשָׁמִים?
phrases.english: Does it teach 'in the summer days and in the rainy days'?
In the sun, because of the sun,
and in the rain, because of the rain, it teaches:
in the days of Nisan and the days of Tishrei,
when there is sun, and there is rain,
and there is honey.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to an earlier issue in the sugya (before this section): the seasons mentioned in the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Careful reading of the exact wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא spoke of summer and winter, when there is no honey.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא speaks of Nisan and Tishrei, when there is honey in the hive.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: a vessel may be placed under a leak
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: on שבת you may put a vessel under a leak.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one may place a vessel under a leak on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to a new line of the משנה. This step sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה allows putting a container under dripping water on שבת to catch it. The גמרא quotes it so it can add details about this case.

phrases.english: And one may place a vessel under a leak on Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the beehive topic and quotes a new line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On שבת, one may put a vessel under a leak.

steps.title: A full vessel may be emptied and put back again and again
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא adds that when the vessel fills up, one may pour it out and put it back, as many times as needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: If the vessel filled up, he pours it out and does it again, and he does not need to hold back.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא adds a detail to the משנה's rule. You are not limited to one vesselful of water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might think the leniency covers only putting the vessel down once. The ברייתא says you may keep emptying and replacing it with no limit.

keyTerms.meaning: He pours out and does it again

phrases.english: It was taught: If the vessel became full,
he pours it out and repeats, and does not hold back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds detail to the משנה quoted in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A full vessel under a leak may be emptied and put back as many times as needed.

steps.title: אביי's leaking millhouse and רבה's advice
steps.stepSummary: אביי's millhouse leaked. רבה told him to bring his bed into the room, so the water would count like a chamber pot, and then take the water out.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי's millhouse leaked. He came before רבה. רבה said to him: Go bring your bed in there, so the water will be like a chamber pot, and then take it out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about a leak on שבת. רבה gives אביי a way to be allowed to remove the water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the water may not simply be carried out. A גרף של רעי (chamber pot) may be taken out of a room where people are, because it is disgusting to them. By making the millhouse a place where he sleeps, אביי makes the dirty water count like a chamber pot, so he may remove it.
steps.whatToRemember: A disgusting thing in a room where people live may be removed on שבת, like a chamber pot. רבה used this rule to let אביי clear out the leaking water.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a practical, permitted way to deal with damage on שבת: changing the situation so that an existing leniency applies.

phrases.english: Abaye's millhouse leaked.
He came before Rabba.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: זִיל עַיְּילֵיהּ לְפוּרְיָךְ לְהָתָם,
phrases.english: He said to him: Go bring your bed in there,
so that it will be like a chamber pot,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the dirty water. A chamber pot may be taken out of a room people use, and now the water counts the same way.

phrases.english: and take it out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A real-life story about a leak on שבת, continuing the topic of steps 5-6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: By bringing his bed into the leaking room, אביי makes the dirty water like a chamber pot, which may be removed.

steps.title: אביי questions רבה's advice
steps.stepSummary: אביי wonders whether one may create a גרף של רעי on purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי sat and found it difficult: may one make a chamber pot situation on purpose, from the start?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי sits and thinks about רבה's advice from the last step, and he has a problem with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The heter to remove a גרף של רעי is for a mess that is already there. רבה's plan was to bring the bed in so the water would become a גרף של רעי on purpose. אביי asks if it is right to set up such a heter לכתחילה.

keyTerms.meaning: a chamber pot; something disgusting that may be removed on שבת

phrases.english: Abaye sat, and it was difficult for him:

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי עוֹשִׂין גְּרָף שֶׁל רְעִי לְכַתְּחִלָּה?
phrases.english: May one make a chamber pot from the start?
phrases.notes: He means creating the disgusting situation on purpose just so you are allowed to remove it, like רבה's plan with the bed in Step 7.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבה's advice given in Step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's advice to bring the bed into the leaking millhouse
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The heter of גרף של רעי seems meant for a mess that already exists, not one made on purpose.

steps.title: The millhouse collapses and אביי accepts the lesson
steps.stepSummary: While אביי was still thinking it over, his millhouse fell, and he said he got this for going against his teacher.
steps.simpleTranslation: Meanwhile, אביי's millhouse collapsed. He said: I had this coming, because I went against the word of my master.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends: as אביי was still questioning the advice, the millhouse collapsed, and he blamed himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קשיא is not answered with a logical argument. Instead the story teaches a lesson about respect: אביי sees the collapse as the result of questioning רבה instead of just following him.

keyTerms.meaning: let it come upon me; I deserved this

steps.whatToRemember: The story of אביי's millhouse ends with אביי accepting that he should have followed רבה's advice.

phrases.english: Meanwhile, Abaye's millhouse fell down.
He said: Let it come upon me,
for I went against the word of my master.
phrases.notes: "My master" is his teacher רבה, who gave the advice.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes אביי's question with what happened next instead of with an answer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אביי admits he should not have questioned רבה's ruling.

steps.title: שמואל: taking out chamber pots on שבת
steps.stepSummary: שמואל permits taking a chamber pot or urine pot out to the garbage heap. When bringing it back, one puts water in it first.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: A container of excrement and a container of urine may be taken out to the garbage heap. When he brings it back, he puts water in it and brings it back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling from שמואל about moving disgusting containers on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Going out, the waste may be removed because it is disgusting. Coming back, the container is empty, so שמואל says to put water in it before carrying it back.

phrases.english: Shmuel said:

phrases.aramaic: גְּרָף שֶׁל רְעִי וְעָבִיט שֶׁל מֵימֵי רַגְלַיִם —
phrases.english: A container of excrement and a container of urine:
it is permitted to take them out to the garbage heap,
and when he brings it back,
he puts water in it and brings it back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from אביי's story to a general rule about moving chamber pots.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A chamber pot may be carried out to the garbage heap and brought back with water in it.

steps.title: A first reading: only together with the container
steps.stepSummary: Some understood from שמואל that the waste may be moved only inside its container, not by itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: They understood from this: a chamber pot together with the vessel, yes; by itself, no.
steps.whatsHappening: Some people read שמואל's ruling and drew a limit from it. The גמרא is setting this up so it can test it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל spoke about a container, so they thought the heter only applies when the dirt is moved along with a vessel. Picking up the disgusting thing directly would then be forbidden.

phrases.english: They understood from it:

phrases.aramaic: גְּרָף שֶׁל רְעִי, אַגַּב מָנָא — אִין,
phrases.english: A chamber pot, together with the vessel: yes,
by itself: no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a limit from the wording of שמואל in Step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: First reading: disgusting things may be removed only inside a vessel.

steps.title: רב אשי and the mouse in the spice storeroom
steps.stepSummary: A mouse was found in רב אשי's spice storeroom, and he told them to hold it by its tail and take it out. So a disgusting thing may be removed even by itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: a mouse was found in רב אשי's spice storeroom. רב אשי said to them: Hold it by its tail and take it out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story that knocks down the reading from Step 11.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mouse was not in any vessel, yet רב אשי let them carry it out directly. So the heter is not limited to moving dirt inside a container; the disgusting thing itself may be removed.

keyTerms.meaning: come and hear; a source is being brought

steps.whatToRemember: Something disgusting may be removed on שבת even directly, not only inside a vessel.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
that a certain mouse
was found in Rav Ashi's spice storeroom.
Rav Ashi said to them:
Hold it by its tail and take it out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the limit proposed in Step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea that disgusting things may only be moved inside a vessel
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב אשי allowed a mouse to be carried out directly, with no vessel.

steps.title: New משנה: what is forbidden on שבת is forbidden on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: Anything forbidden on שבת because of שבות, רשות, or מצוה is forbidden on יום טוב too.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Anything one is liable for on שבת because of שבות, because of רשות, or because of מצוה, one is liable for it on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It sets out a general rule, and its examples come after this opening line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יום טוב allows some food preparation, but that does not mean rabbinic rules are relaxed. The דרבנן rules of שבת, called שבות, רשות, and מצוה, apply on יום טוב in the same way.

keyTerms.meaning: a rabbinic rule to keep the day restful
something optional; not a full מצוה

steps.confusionAlert: "Because of מצוה" does not mean doing a מצוה is forbidden. It means the act has a מצוה side to it, and still the חכמים forbade it on שבת, and so on יום טוב.

phrases.english: Mishnah:
Anything one is liable for because of shevut,
phrases.notes: שבות is a rabbinic rule made to keep the day restful.

phrases.english: because of reshut, because of מצוה,
on Shabbat, one is liable for it on Yom Tov.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the discussion of leaks and chamber pots.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rabbinic שבת restrictions (שבות, רשות, מצוה) apply on יום טוב as well.

steps.title: The list of things forbidden because of שבות
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists acts the חכמים forbade as a שבות: climbing a tree, riding an animal, swimming, clapping, slapping the thigh, and dancing.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are forbidden because of שבות: one may not climb a tree, ride an animal, swim, clap hands, slap the thigh, or dance.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives examples of the first group from the last step: things the חכמים forbade as a שבות, a rabbinic rest rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: None of these acts is a real מלאכה from the תורה. The חכמים forbade them to keep the day restful and to keep people away from real מלאכה. This step only gives the list; it does not give reasons.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic rule of rest, not a תורה-level מלאכה
Slapping the hand on the thigh

phrases.english: And these are the ones forbidden because of שבות:
One may not climb a tree,
nor ride on an animal,
nor swim on the water,
nor clap, nor slap,
nor dance.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in the first category (שבות) named in step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Climbing trees, riding animals, swimming, clapping, thigh-slapping, and dancing are forbidden as שבות.

steps.title: The list of things forbidden even though they are optional good deeds
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists acts in the רשות group: judging, making קידושין, doing חליצה, and doing יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are forbidden even though they are רשות: one may not judge, betroth a woman, do חליצה, or do יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives examples of the second group: acts that have a good-deed side but are optional, and are still forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point of this group is that you might think these acts should be allowed because they have some value. The משנה teaches that they are still forbidden on שבת and יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: Optional; an act with some good-deed value but not a full obligation
Doing חליצה, the release ceremony instead of יבום
Doing יבום, marrying a brother's childless widow

phrases.english: And these are the ones forbidden even though they are optional:
One may not judge, nor betroth a woman,
nor do חליצה, nor do יבום.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in the second category (רשות) named in step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Judging, קידושין, חליצה, and יבום are forbidden on שבת and יום טוב.

steps.title: The list of things forbidden even though they are full מצוות
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists acts in the מצוה group: dedicating to the מקדש, ערכין vows, חרמים, and separating תרומה and מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are forbidden even though they are a מצוה: one may not dedicate items to the מקדש, make an ערכין vow, declare a חרם, or separate תרומה and מעשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives examples of the third group: acts that are real מצוות, yet still may not be done on these days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This group goes one step further than רשות. Even a full מצוה act is forbidden here. So a good-deed value alone does not make an act allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Making an ערכין vow, pledging a person's set value
The portion of produce given to a כהן

phrases.english: And these are the ones forbidden even though they are a מצוה:
One may not dedicate to the מקדש, nor make an ערכין vow,
phrases.notes: The ערכין vow is described in ויקרא 27.

phrases.english: nor declare something חרם,
nor separate תרומה and מעשר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in the third category (מצוה), going further than the רשות list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הקדש, ערכין, חרמים, and separating תרומה and מעשר are forbidden on שבת and יום טוב.

steps.title: Summary: all of this applies on יום טוב and even more on שבת; only food preparation differs
steps.stepSummary: All these were said about יום טוב, so they apply all the more on שבת. The only difference between יום טוב and שבת is preparing food.
steps.simpleTranslation: All these were said about יום טוב, and by a קל וחומר they apply on שבת. There is no difference between יום טוב and שבת except for preparing food.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה wraps up the lists. It says they apply on יום טוב and even more on שבת, and gives the general rule about how the two days compare.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שבת is stricter than יום טוב, so whatever is forbidden on יום טוב is surely forbidden on שבת. The one thing allowed on יום טוב but not on שבת is מלאכה needed for food (אוכל נפש).

keyTerms.meaning: An argument from a lighter case to a stricter one
Food preparation for eating, allowed on יום טוב

steps.whatToRemember: שבות, רשות, and מצוה acts are forbidden on both שבת and יום טוב. The only difference between the days is אוכל נפש, which is allowed on יום טוב.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as saying the days are the same in every way. The משנה names one real difference: food preparation is allowed on יום טוב but not on שבת.

phrases.english: All these were said about יום טוב,
all the more so on שבת.
There is no difference between יום טוב and שבת
except for food preparation alone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Summarizes the three lists and states the general rule comparing יום טוב and שבת.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Everything listed applies on יום טוב and even more on שבת; the only difference between the days is אוכל נפש.

steps.title: Why climbing a tree is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: Climbing a tree is forbidden because a person might pull off a branch or leaf.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: We don't climb a tree. This is a decree, in case he pulls something off.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining the משנה's list of שבות acts. It starts with climbing a tree and gives the reason the חכמים forbade it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Climbing a tree is not a מלאכה by itself. The worry is that while climbing, a person may snap off a branch, leaf, or fruit. Pulling something off a growing plant is the תורה-level מלאכה of קוצר (reaping).

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
A protective decree of the חכמים, made to keep people away from a real Torah prohibition
He will pull off (detach something growing)

steps.confusionAlert: The act itself, climbing, is not a מלאכה from the תורה. The decree protects against a different act, pulling off something growing, which could easily happen along the way.

phrases.english: GEMARA: We do not climb a tree —
a decree, lest he detach [something].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא's explanation of the שבות list given in the משנה (step 14).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Climbing a tree is forbidden as a גזירה, in case one detaches something and does the מלאכה of reaping.

steps.title: First reason for not riding an animal
steps.stepSummary: Riding an animal is forbidden in case the rider goes past the תחום, the שבת boundary.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we don't ride on an animal. This is a decree, in case he goes outside the תחום.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a first reason for the ban on riding an animal: a rider might travel beyond the שבת boundary without noticing. This reason sets up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On an animal you cover distance quickly and easily, so you could pass the 2,000-אמה limit without realizing it. The decree would be a fence around the law of תחומין.

keyTerms.meaning: Outside the שבת boundary (beyond the area one may walk on שבת or יום טוב)

phrases.english: And we do not ride on the back of an animal —
a decree, lest he go outside the boundary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next item in the משנה's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Proposed reason: riding is forbidden in case one leaves the תחום.

steps.title: That reason would make תחומין a דאורייתא law
steps.stepSummary: If the חכמים made a fence around תחומין, that would show תחומין are from the תורה, and that is not accepted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this that תחומין are from the תורה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects to the reason just given. If it were true, it would prove something we do not want to prove: that the law of תחומין comes from the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים usually do not build a decree on top of another decree. If they had to protect תחומין with a decree, the תחום law itself would have to be from the תורה. Whether תחומין are from the תורה is a disputed question, so this reason cannot simply be taken for granted.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this (here used as a challenge: "so you'd have to conclude...!")
The laws of the שבת boundary

steps.confusionAlert: Though it looks like a statement, "שמע מינה" here is a challenge. The גמרא is not concluding that תחומין are from the תורה. It is pointing out that this reason would force that conclusion.

phrases.english: Learn from this that boundaries are from the Torah!
phrases.notes: The חכמים don't usually make a fence around their own rule, so this reason would only fit if תחומין were from the תורה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reason given in step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reason that riding is forbidden in case one leaves the תחום.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A protective decree around תחומין only makes sense if תחומין are a Torah law. That is a disputed claim, so this reason cannot simply be assumed.

steps.title: New reason: he might cut a branch
steps.stepSummary: The real reason is that a rider might cut a branch from a tree to use as a whip.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is a decree in case he cuts off a branch.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the תחום reason and gives a new one. A rider might break off a branch to drive the animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cutting a branch is reaping, a תורה-level מלאכה. With this reason the decree protects a תורה law directly, so the problem from step 20 goes away. The גמרא no longer has to decide whether תחומין are from the תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (drops the earlier idea and replaces it)

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the גמרא is careful to pick reasons that do not quietly decide other open questions, such as whether תחומין come from the תורה.

phrases.english: Rather: a decree, lest he cut off a branch.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 20 by replacing the reason from step 19.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Riding is forbidden in case one leaves the תחום, which would make תחומין a Torah law.
steps.terutzMaskana: Riding is forbidden in case one cuts a branch, which is the Torah מלאכה of reaping.

steps.title: Why swimming is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: Swimming is forbidden in case a person makes a swimmer's float.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we don't swim on the water. This is a decree, in case he makes a swimmer's barrel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the next item on the list, swimming. The worry is that he will build a float to help him swim.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Swimming is not a מלאכה. But someone who wants to swim might put together a floating device, and making a usable object counts as forbidden מלאכה.

phrases.english: And we do not swim on the surface of the water —

phrases.aramaic: גְּזֵרָה שֶׁמָּא יַעֲשֶׂה חָבִית שֶׁל שַׁיָּיטִין.
phrases.english: a decree, lest he make a swimmers' barrel.
phrases.notes: A floating device that beginners hold on to while learning to swim.

steps.triggerLanguage: גְּזֵרָה שֶׁמָּא יַעֲשֶׂה חָבִית שֶׁל שַׁיָּיטִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to going through the משנה's list after the side discussion about riding.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Swimming is forbidden as a גזירה, in case one makes a swimming float.

steps.title: Why clapping and dancing are forbidden
steps.stepSummary: Clapping, slapping the thigh, and dancing are forbidden in case a person fixes a musical instrument.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we don't clap, slap the thigh, or dance. This is a decree, in case he fixes a musical instrument.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the list with one reason covering three acts. All of them could lead a person to fix a musical instrument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Clapping, slapping, and dancing go along with music. When people are caught up in the music, they may repair an instrument to play along. Fixing a usable object is a תורה-level מלאכה.

keyTerms.meaning: Slap the hand on the thigh

steps.whatToRemember: Every act in the שבות list is a גזירה, a fence the חכמים built so a person won't slip into a real מלאכה from the תורה. Climbing a tree or riding could lead to reaping. Swimming could lead to making a float. Clapping and dancing could lead to fixing an instrument.

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא מְטַפְּחִין וְלֹא מְסַפְּקִין וְלֹא מְרַקְּדִין —
phrases.english: And we do not clap, nor slap the thigh, nor dance —
a decree, lest he fix musical instruments.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes explaining the last items in the משנה's שבות list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Clapping, thigh-slapping, and dancing are forbidden as a גזירה, in case one fixes a musical instrument.

steps.title: The optional-acts list begins with judging
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's second list, acts forbidden משום רשות, beginning with 'one may not judge'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And these are forbidden because they are optional acts: one may not judge.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting the next part of the משנה to set up a question about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 18-23 explained the items forbidden משום שבות. Now the משנה starts a new group called רשות, meaning things that are optional and not full obligations. The first item in this group is judging a court case.

keyTerms.meaning: And these are; it opens a new list
Because they are optional acts, not full obligations
Judging, serving as a judge in a court case

phrases.english: And these are forbidden because they are optional:
One may not judge.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the שבות list (steps 18-23) to the next list in the משנה, the רשות items.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Judging is forbidden on שבת and יום טוב, and the משנה lists it as a רשות, an optional act.

steps.title: Judging is a real מצוה, so why call it optional?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: a judge does a real מצוה, so why does the משנה call judging only רשות?
steps.simpleTranslation: But he is doing a מצוה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's label. Judging seems like a full מצוה, not just an optional act.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem is the category the משנה chose. Judging fairly is a real מצוה, so it seems it should be listed under מצוה and not under רשות. The גמרא is not asking whether judging is forbidden. It is asking why it is placed in this group.

phrases.english: But he is doing a מצוה!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the רשות label that step 24 gave to judging.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's choice to call judging רשות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Judging is a real מצוה, so calling it optional seems wrong.

steps.title: When someone better is available, judging is optional
steps.stepSummary: The משנה means a case where another person is better qualified to judge, so this judge's act is only optional.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed for a case where there is someone better than him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה is talking about a specific case: someone more qualified than this judge is available.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In general, judging is a מצוה. But if a better judge can handle the case, then this person does not have to judge. So for him it is only רשות. The answer keeps judging a מצוה in general and explains the label by narrowing the case.

keyTerms.meaning: It is only needed for; it tells us the case is a specific one

phrases.english: No, it is needed
where there is someone better than him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 25 by limiting the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Judging is always a full מצוה, so it should not be called רשות.
steps.terutzMaskana: When someone better can judge, this person's judging is only optional, so it fits under רשות.
steps.whatToRemember: Judging is called רשות in the משנה because the case is one where a better judge is available.

steps.title: The next optional act: betrothing a woman
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next item in the רשות list: one may not betroth a woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one may not betroth a woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next item in the משנה's list to set up the same kind of question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Betrothal (קידושין) is also listed as רשות. Once again the label will be questioned, just as it was for judging.

phrases.english: And one may not betroth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next item in the same רשות list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Betrothing a woman is forbidden on שבת and יום טוב, and it is listed as רשות.

steps.title: Betrothal is a real מצוה, so why call it optional?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks the same question as before: a man who marries does a מצוה, so why is it called רשות?
steps.simpleTranslation: But he is doing a מצוה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the label again, this time for betrothal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Marrying makes it possible to keep the מצוה of פריה ורביה, having children. So betrothal seems like a real מצוה and not just an optional act. This is the same challenge, word for word, as step 25.

keyTerms.meaning: But surely; it opens a challenge

phrases.english: But he is doing a מצוה!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the challenge of step 25, now aimed at betrothal.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's choice to call betrothal רשות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Marrying is connected to the מצוה of פריה ורביה, so it should count as a מצוה.

steps.title: The answer begins: a specific case is meant
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts to answer with 'לא צריכא', which shows the משנה is speaking about a specific case. The case itself is given in the continuing text.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer, the same way it did for judging. The details of the case come in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The opening 'לא צריכא' shows the answer will again limit the case. It will explain when betrothal counts as only optional. That case is not given in these words; it continues right after.

keyTerms.meaning: It is only needed for; it tells us a specific case is coming

phrases.english: No, it is needed

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to the challenge of step 28.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא); the details continue in the next lines
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Betrothal is always a full מצוה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה must be speaking about a specific case where betrothal is only optional. That case is given in the continuing text.
